features.description: Observe the next few real tasks, prune noisy topics, and add missing query paths only where agents still drift or over-read.
features.evidence: Used real repo-maintenance tasks on 2026-07-09 through 2026-07-11 to tighten the harness five ways: first by switching Node workspace defaults from pnpm to npm, then by adding explicit Before state, After state, Regression test results, PR ready, and CI ready checkpoints to `AGENTS.md`, `.repo-harness/topics/agent-workflow.md`, `progress.md`, and `session-handoff.md`, then by recreating the isolated-modules migration handoff as an in-repo artifact at `isolated-modules-migration-handoff.md`, then by executing that migration: removing the root Node workspace file, moving active Node modules to module-local `package-lock.json` plus `npm ci --include=dev`, eliminating shared `workspace` and shared TS-config assumptions, and verifying representative modules through `./scripts/module ci`, and finally by using a live `xq-kraken` review/fix task to confirm the harness supports narrow module work while documenting a contract correction in `modules/xq-kraken/model/api_catalog.py` and `modules/xq-kraken/API_CATALOG_CONTRACT.md`.

features.name: Onboard xq-fitness-mobile
features.description: Register the private Expo fitness app with build-and-unit CI, local integration testing, and local physical-device verification while excluding simulator workflows.
features.evidence: Registered the module with canonical 2.0.0 versioning, build-and-unit-only CI, local integration orchestration, and environment-driven physical-device commands. `./scripts/module ci xq-fitness-mobile` passed with 10 suites/75 tests; local integration passed with 10 suites/61 tests and clean teardown. Final device acceptance is blocked because CoreDevice could not detect the dedicated device; the Expo implementation is now a frozen behavior reference for feat-011.

features.name: Native offline XQ Fitness foundation
features.description: Create the native SwiftUI fitness app with MVVM plus Router, a versioned local-only store, and the empty-state-to-create-routine flow while retaining the Expo app as a frozen behavior reference.
features.evidence: Added and registered `ios-xq-fitness-app` with SwiftUI MVVM plus Router, a versioned local FitnessStore, JSON primary/recovery persistence, an in-memory adapter, empty-first routine UI, and routine creation. `./scripts/module ci ios-xq-fitness-app` passed an unsigned generic-iOS build and 9 host-side unit tests on 2026-07-13; no simulator or API surface was added.

features.name: Physical-device fitness E2E coverage
features.description: Add consumer-owned XCUITest journeys for every behavior in the native fitness foundation and validate them locally on the connected iPhone without adding simulator or CI execution.
features.evidence: Added the consumer-owned `ios-xq-fitness-appUITests` target, XQUIHarness screen objects, guarded isolated reset, four routine-flow E2E journeys, and a local environment-driven device runner. The complete suite passed 4/4 with 0 failures on the connected iPhone 12 running iOS 26.5; `./scripts/module ci ios-xq-fitness-app` also passed the generic iOS build and 11 unit tests. CI remains build-and-unit-only, with no simulator or committed device identifier.

features.name: Seven-day routines and snapshot comparison
features.description: Give every native routine exactly seven training days, support local exercise management within each day, and compare each new immutable snapshot with the previous snapshot using old-app-style progress indicators.
features.evidence: Added schema-v2 migration to exactly seven stable days, local add/update/delete exercise commands, immutable snapshot capture, case-insensitive highest-value aggregation, and First/Increased/Decreased/Same comparison for reps and weight. Added full SwiftUI drill-down and a fifth physical-device journey. `./scripts/module ci ios-xq-fitness-app` passed the generic build and 16 unit tests; XCResult reports 5/5 E2E tests passed on iPhone 12 / iOS 26.5.

features.name: Snapshot retention coverage matrix
features.description: Retain only the newest two routine snapshots, prove immediate-previous comparison through host and physical-device tests, and document component-by-capability coverage with unit/UI ownership per cell.
features.evidence: TDD proved the retention boundary: the RED tracer observed A/B/C where B/C was required, then the store was changed to atomically retain only the newest two snapshots. The new host test proves B/C retention and C-versus-B reporting; the extended physical-device journey proves 10 → 20 → 15 reps yields Decreased and remains Decreased after relaunch. The component × capability matrix records unit/UI ownership and explicit gaps. `./scripts/module ci ios-xq-fitness-app` passed the generic build and all 17 host tests; XCResult reports 5 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped on iPhone 12 / iOS 26.5.

features.name: UI coverage gap and clean-test isolation
features.description: Cover exercise deletion through the physical-device UI and make every fitness UI test begin from a reset, verified-empty test-only store through one shared test interface.
features.evidence: Added a RED-to-GREEN physical-device tracer for exercise swipe deletion and introduced `FitnessUITestCase`, whose shared setup resets the isolated store and requires the empty routine list before every test body. Persistence journeys now explicitly relaunch while preserving data. Generic UI build-for-testing passed, module CI passed the generic build plus 17 host tests, the delete tracer passed, and the complete clean-state suite passed 6/6 with 0 failures on iPhone 12 / iOS 26.5.

features.name: Unambiguous exercise input labels
features.description: Give every exercise input a persistent visible label and cover the labels through a clean-state physical-device UI test.
features.evidence: TDD RED failed on-device because the visible Exercise name label did not exist. Replaced placeholder-only rows with persistent Exercise name, Sets, Repetitions, and Weight (kg) labels while preserving field identifiers, defaults, keyboards, and save behavior. PR review tightened coverage to assert the exact visible/accessibility label values and every exact Day 1–7 row. The final clean-state device suite passed 7/7 in 298.892 seconds, module CI passed the generic build plus 17 host tests, and PR #24 merged into main at 1468e25579fc608e715142cec2fead885f0f0ca6 after all eight GitHub checks passed on 2026-07-14.

features.name: Local signed IPA deployment helper
features.description: Provide a module-local script to archive, export, validate, install, and launch the native fitness app on a registered physical iPhone.
features.evidence: Added modules/ios-xq-fitness-app/scripts/build-device-ipa.sh with automatic development signing, requested hardware-UDID default 00008150-0012058A14F8401C, CoreDevice UUID override support, provisioning validation, diagnostic device-list output, installation/launch, no project regeneration that can erase Xcode signing settings, and documented overrides. Added the legacy XQ Fitness AppIcon asset and replaced numeric training-day labels with Monday through Sunday, including visible MON through SUN badges, while preserving stable numeric IDs and migrating legacy Day N names. bash -n, --help, git diff --check, direct native build, 17 host tests, and ./init.sh passed on 2026-07-15. Signed archive/export succeeded and the updated IPA installed on 00008150-0012058A14F8401C; automatic launch was denied only because the device was locked.
